problems: The title and the 'cord' never show up as a cord on the cart. In storyboard frames 1-6 and the 25% still, a thin line runs from the clay pots toward the tree and maybe to the back of the cart, but you can't tell where it attaches. From frame 7 on, and in the 50% and 75% stills, no cord trails behind the cart at all, so whatever powered it is either cut or was never connected.

Nothing shows that the drum motor drives the cart. In every frame the black drum on the deck looks the same: no visible spin, belt, axle link or cord paying out. The cart just rolls, with no visible cause.

The camera stays locked on the cart for all 16 frames, so the cart sits frozen in the same spot on screen and the only sign it moves is the planks and flowers sliding past. You never see it start from rest beside the pots (frame 1 already looks like a scrolling shot) or stop. The film just ends mid-roll in frame 16, so the motion has no start and no end.

The 'six clay pots' are never all in view: the right edge of the frame cuts them off in frames 1-4 and the 25% still, and by frame 8 they're gone. A viewer can't count six or tell what the pots with blue liquid are for.

At the 25% and 75% stills the near front wheel hangs over the edge of the board, and its rim drops below the plank top instead of resting on it. The wheel looks partly sunk into or in front of the plank road, not rolling on it.

The giant brown trunk takes up the top right of frames 1-6, and the road is cut in half by a hard shadow band. Most of each frame is empty sand and grass, while the subject, the motor, is a small dark lump.
posts.critique: It's a nicely made wooden cart sliding through a pretty meadow, but the cord in the title and the motor in the caption do nothing you can see. With the camera locked on the cart, it reads as a parked cart with the scenery scrolling behind it, and it has no start and no end.
